subject.title: fix(coding-agent): scope CODEX_HOME to prevent OAuth collision with OpenClaw

question: Should the coding-agent's isolated worker home intentionally start as a completely clean Codex profile, or must selected non-auth configuration from the user's existing Codex home remain available?
rationale: `CODEX_HOME` is the ownership boundary for credentials and all other Codex profile state, so the patch cannot isolate only OAuth without choosing and documenting a compatibility policy for existing worker configuration.

options.title: Preserve selected worker settings
options.body: Add a safe initialization or migration path for explicitly selected non-auth configuration while excluding all ambient authentication material.

options.title: Adopt a clean worker profile
options.body: Intentionally reset all Codex worker customization, clearly document the upgrade impact, and provide proof of the clean-profile workflow.

options.title: Pause the isolation change
options.body: Keep the current launch path until a supported profile-initialization policy can be agreed and demonstrated.

recommendation.title: Preserve selected worker settings
recommendation.body: Add a safe initialization or migration path for explicitly selected non-auth configuration while excluding all ambient authentication material.

likelyOwner.reason: The coding-agent history shows the strongest sustained ownership signal for its launch and compatibility policy.
